thread:
mia.design: Heads up — dropped a new compact preview interaction in Figma. Focus is hover/keyboard parity and screen-reader announcements. link: https://www.figma.com/file/XXXXxx (see frames: compact-preview / hover-states)

sam.pm: Nice. Main question — when a user hovers the channel preview should we show the suppression toggle inline or in a tiny overlay? Hover overlay might be clipped on narrow panels.

mia.design: Leaning overlay for discoverability but it needs an accessible fallback. If overlay is used, keyboard should open it with Enter/Space when focus is on the preview row.

ash.eng: Overlay's doable, but we need a clear focus trap so tabbing doesn't land behind the preview. Suggest roving tabindex on rows and `aria-expanded` on the preview button rather than a full modal.

aria.access: For SRs, when preview expands announce "Channel preview expanded: [channel name], suppression off/on" via `aria-live="polite"`. Also ensure the overlay has `role="dialog"` and `aria-modal="false"` (since it's non-blocking).

lisa.product: Copy note: we keep debating "quiet window" vs "snooze window". Ops teams prefer "quiet window" but some users think "snooze" is clearer. Can we test with customers?

mia.design: Good call. For the compact view I added microcopy: "Quiet window (silences channel notifications)" — short helptext on hover. Thoughts?

sam.pm: Keep it short in the row. Maybe tooltip with full explanation. In the preview drawer we can show the long-form.

ash.eng: Implementation nit: if we animate the overlay, screen readers may get the announcement before content is visible. Add a 50–100ms delay before sending `aria-live` or ensure content is appended before announcing.

aria.access: Exactly. Alternatively, update a visually-hidden DOM node after overlay render and then set `aria-live`. Example pattern:

```
// after overlay mount
setTimeout(() => {
  liveRegion.textContent = `Preview opened for ${channelName}, suppression ${state}`;
}, 60);
```

mia.design: Thanks — I'll add that snippet to the handoff notes. Also need contrast check: the preview badge background (#F5F7FF) + text (#6B7280) fails AA at 12px.

lisa.product: Oof — can we bump badge weight or change BG to slightly darker? Prefer not to increase font size in compact rows.

ash.eng: We can switch badge BG to #EEF2FF and increase contrast by using #374151 for text. That keeps visual hierarchy. I'll include tokens.

aria.access: Keyboard focus ring needs to be 3px for the compact rows to meet 3:1 contrast with the bg when using the darker token. Also ensure high-contrast mode picks up system outlines.

mia.design: I'll update the Figma tokens (compact-badge-bg / compact-badge-text / focus-ring) and push a handoff file.

sam.pm: One more UX flow: when a user toggles suppression from the preview, do we show an inline confirmation toast or change the pill state immediately? Rapid toggles could cause accidental silences.

lisa.product: Show immediate state change but add a small undo toast: "Channel silenced — Undo" with 6s timeout. Keeps it fast but reversible.

ash.eng: Implementable. We'll base undo via optimistic update + server confirm. If server fails, show error toast and revert.

aria.access: For the toast, use `role="status"` and make sure the Undo action is keyboard focusable and announced as part of the toast.

mia.design: Great. I'll incorporate these decisions into the final handoff: overlay w/ keyboard activation, aria-live delay pattern, updated tokens for badge contrast, copy variants for research (quiet vs snooze), and undo toast behavior.

mia.design: Anyone object to me creating a small usability test (3 tasks) to settle "quiet" vs "snooze" wording before dev starts?

lisa.product: Go for it — I'll prep 2 quick survey questions to use in the test.

aria.access: I'll review the test script for a11y scenarios (screen reader + keyboard-only).

a11y-bot: Reminder: add `data-testid` attributes to preview controls for automated accessibility smoke tests.

mia.design: Will do — thanks all. I'll push updated frames and the handoff checklist by EOD.
